The toxic algae crisis in Lake Okeechobee underscores systemic failures in water management and agricultural runoff oversight. While the DOH advisories rightly warn residents to avoid contaminated waters (microcystin levels at 0.58 ppb with EPA's danger threshold at 8 ppb), the root issue remains unaddressed: decades of nutrient pollution from industrial farms flooding the lake with nitrogen and phosphorus.

Taxpayer-funded agencies like DEP collect samples and publish dashboards, but where’s the accountability for upstream polluters? The Army Corps’ current pause on discharges to the C-44 Canal doesn’t fix the underlying problem—Florida’s water infrastructure still prioritizes Big Ag’s interests over public health.

Until Washington enforces strict nutrient limits and overhauls outdated drainage systems, these toxic blooms will keep threatening ecosystems, tourism, and families relying on these waters.

Declaration of the American Veteran

“Not to find out new principles, or new arguments, never before thought of, not merely to say things which had never been said before; but to place before mankind the common sense of the subject; terms so plain and firm as to command their assent, and to justify ourselves in the independent stand we were compelled to take… it was intended to be an expression of the American mind, and give to that expression the proper tone and spirit called for by the occasion.”
— Thomas Jefferson

We, our Nation’s Veterans — 

your sons and daughters, 
mothers and fathers, 
sisters and brothers — 

declare that our long patience has been met only with betrayal. 

We do not seek novelty, nor the reinvention of principle, but to place before our fellow citizens
the plain common sense of the matter.

We have been patient. 
We have been reasonable. 
We have petitioned, 
testified, 
waited, 
and pleaded.

And 
“our repeated petitions have been answered only by repeated injury.”

The Department of Veterans Affairs was founded to serve those who served. 
Yet its record is one of delay, denial, and disdain.

The VA has delayed care until illness became permanent, 
until wounds grew irreparable, 
until lives were lost.

The VA has falsified records and hidden failures, burying truth with the bodies of those it failed.

The VA has known of the suicide epidemic, 
yet distorted the numbers, concealed the scale, 

and watched as more than forty Veterans a day — over sixteen thousand a year — 
took their own lives, 
casualties not of war, but of betrayal.

The VA has silenced dissent, 
branding Veterans who demand justice as “disruptive,” and targeting whistleblowers with retaliation, intimidation, and ruin.

The VA has allowed corruption and incompetence to endure, 
while those responsible faced no justice.

These are not the errors of a day, nor the failings of a few. 
They are a system sustained by neglect,
insulated by bureaucracy, 
and deaf for decades to the very voices it was built to serve and care for.

Let it be clear: we name not an enemy but a failing institution. 
We extend once more the hand of partnership. 
Yet partnership requires truth, 
and truth demands change.

If the People’s representatives, the press, and our fellow citizens stand with us,
let them speak and act.
Let them show where THEY stand, 
and who THEY are.

But know this: whether joined or abandoned,
we will act. 
For we are still what we have always been — 
sentinels of this grand Republic, 
guardians of its promises, 
and brothers and sisters to one another.

We do not ask permission to live with dignity.
We claim it.

And in so doing, we draw this line: 
that never again will Veterans be left to die in silence, or live in neglect, 
while those sworn to serve them look away.

Runoff’s Toxic Impact on Our Ecosystems & Health 🌍🚨
Runoff—loaded with nitrates, phosphates, glyphosates, pesticides like paraquat, & heavy metals—comes from lawns, golf courses, farms, & urban areas. It fuels algal blooms (Bocas & Blue Cypress Lake), killing seagrass (50% gone since 1950s, FL DEP) & starving manatees (25% died, Save the Manatee). #EcoCrisis
Golf courses are a major runoff source—pesticides like paraquat & rotenone link to a 126% higher Parkinson’s risk (Medscape, May 2025). Glyphosates in runoff also tied to cancers (Florida Phoenix). This poisons estuaries like the Indian River Lagoon, killing fisheries—70% of FL’s fish rely on seagrass (Drive a Boat USA).
Fire retardants (e.g., Phos-Chek) used in wildfires wash into estuaries, killing salmon & aquatic life (EHN, 2022). In FL, this adds to petrochemicals (fuel spills, EPA) & pharmaceuticals (antibiotics, ACS Chem Reviews) in fisheries, causing chronic harm to fish, oysters, & crabs. Our seafood is at risk!
Antiperspirants with aluminum are linked to dementia & Alzheimer’s—studies show higher brain aluminum in patients (CMSS Chicago, Jan 2025). Runoff carries these chemicals into waterways, compounding the toxic load in estuaries where flamingos once thrived. We’re losing our biodiversity!
Immediate Actions: Ban lawn fertilizers & golf course pesticides (glyphosates, paraquat). Enforce No Wake Zones in inlets, 200 yds of anchored boats, sensitive areas, & grass flats to save manatees. Audit waste (St. Johns Riverkeeper) & install mooring buoys (Bocas model). Contact Sen. Rodriguez now! #NoWakeZone
Long-term Goal: Restore seagrass & water quality to bring back flamingos to FL! It’ll take 10-20 yrs (Science Advances), but cleaner estuaries = thriving fisheries, manatees, & birds. Clearwater crash (1 dead) shows the stakes—why speed in inshore waters? Let’s act for our planet! 🌿🦩 #SaveFlamingos
